title: Two Sum
why: Checking the complement before storing the current number prevents using the same array position twice.

meanings.nums: input array
meanings.target: value we need two numbers to sum to
meanings.i: current index
meanings.seen: map of value → index already visited
meanings.res: returned index pair

title: Add Two Numbers
why: Each column contributes one output digit; the carry becomes part of the next column's sum.

meanings.l1: first input list, digits stored least-significant-first
meanings.l2: second input list, digits stored least-significant-first
meanings.dummy: sentinel node before the result list head
meanings.curr: builder pointer; appends each new result digit node
meanings.carry: carry into the next digit (0 or 1)
meanings.sum: `l1.val + l2.val + carry` for the current position

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
why: Removing characters from the left restores uniqueness before the window can grow again.

meanings.s: input string being scanned
meanings.left: left edge of the window; slides right to drop repeated characters
meanings.right: right edge of the window; advances one character each iteration
meanings.seen: Set of the characters currently inside the window `[left, right]`
meanings.ans: longest window length found so far, `max(ans, right - left + 1)`

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
why: A valid partition puts every left-side value below every right-side value and balances the two halves.

meanings.nums1: First sorted array (the algorithm searches the smaller of the two)
meanings.m: Length of the smaller array `nums1` after any swap
meanings.n: Length of the larger array `nums2` after any swap
meanings.left: Left bound of the partition search on `nums1`
meanings.right: Right bound of the partition search on `nums1`
meanings.i: Number of `nums1` elements placed in the combined left half (the cut in `nums1`)
meanings.j: Number of `nums2` elements in the left half, `half - i` (the cut in `nums2`)
meanings.left1: Largest value left of the cut in `nums1` (`-Infinity` if none)
meanings.right1: Smallest value right of the cut in `nums1` (`+Infinity` if none)
meanings.left2: Largest value left of the cut in `nums2` (`-Infinity` if none)
meanings.right2: Smallest value right of the cut in `nums2` (`+Infinity` if none)

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
why: Matching the two ends extends a palindrome only when the enclosed substring is also a palindrome.

meanings.s: The input string we search for the longest palindromic substring.
meanings.start: Start index of the best palindrome found so far.
meanings.maxLen: Length of the best palindrome found so far (the answer is `s.substring(start, start + maxLen)`).
meanings.expand: Helper arrow function that grows two pointers `l`/`r` outward while the characters match.
meanings.l: Left pointer of the current expansion (moves left, `l--`).
meanings.r: Right pointer of the current expansion (moves right, `r++`).
meanings.i: Loop index; each `i` is tried as both an odd center (`expand(i, i)`) and an even center (`expand(i, i + 1)`).

title: Reverse Integer
why: Peel one decimal digit from the input and append it to the result; check the signed integer boundary.

meanings.x: The working magnitude. Starts as `Math.abs(input)`, then each iteration its last digit is peeled with `x % 10` and removed with `Math.floor(x / 10)`.
meanings.sign: The original sign, `-1` if the input was negative else `1`. Reapplied to `res` after the digits are reversed.
meanings.res: The reversed value, built by `res = res * 10 + (x % 10)`. After sign is reapplied it is bounds-checked against the signed 32-bit range; out of range returns 0.

title: Regular Expression Matching
why: A star can consume zero copies or another matching character; those alternatives explain the DP dependencies.

meanings.s: Input string to match; its characters label the DP table rows.
meanings.p: Pattern (may contain `.` and `*`); its tokens label the DP table columns.
meanings.m: Length of `s` (number of grid rows beyond row 0).
meanings.n: Length of `p` (number of grid columns beyond column 0).
meanings.dp: Boolean `(m+1)×(n+1)` table; `dp[i][j]` is true if `s[0..i)` matches the pattern prefix `p[0..j)`.
meanings.i: Current row index (chars of `s` consumed so far).
meanings.j: Current column index (tokens of `p` consumed so far).

title: Container With Most Water
why: The shorter wall limits the area. Moving the taller wall inward cannot improve the area with that shorter wall fixed.

meanings.left: left pointer
meanings.right: right pointer
meanings.ans: maximum area seen

title: Roman to Integer
why: Subtract a smaller Roman value when it precedes a larger one; otherwise add its value.

meanings.s: The input Roman numeral string being scanned left to right.
meanings.map: Lookup of each Roman symbol to its integer value (`I`=1 … `M`=1000).
meanings.res: The running total; we subtract or add each symbol's value into it.
meanings.i: Current scan index into `s`.

title: Longest Common Prefix
why: A prefix ends at the first column where a string ends or its character differs.

meanings.i: column index
meanings.j: string index

title: 3Sum
why: Fix one sorted value, then move the remaining two pointers according to whether their sum is too small or too large.

meanings.nums: sorted input array
meanings.res: unique triplets that sum to 0
meanings.i: fixed outer index
meanings.left: left pointer
meanings.right: right pointer

title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
why: Each recursion level chooses one letter for the next digit; a complete path becomes one output string.

meanings.map: keypad mapping from each digit to its letters
meanings.res: output list of all complete combination strings
meanings.path: letters chosen so far (one per digit)
meanings.i: index of the digit currently being expanded

title: 4Sum
why: Fix the leading values, then narrow a sorted pair search; skip equal choices to avoid duplicate quadruplets.

meanings.nums: sorted input array
meanings.target: sum every quadruple must reach
meanings.i: first fixed index (outer loop)
meanings.j: second fixed index (inner loop)
meanings.left: left pointer, starts at j + 1
meanings.right: right pointer, starts at the last index
meanings.res: unique quadruples that sum to target

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
why: A fixed gap between two pointers locates the node before the one to remove without knowing the list length first.

meanings.head: head node of the input linked list
meanings.dummy: sentinel node placed before `head` so removing the first node is uniform
meanings.fast: lead pointer; advances `n` nodes ahead to create the gap
meanings.slow: trailing pointer; ends up just before the node to remove
meanings.n: the position from the end of the node to remove (1-indexed)

title: Valid Parentheses
why: The latest unmatched opening bracket must match the next closing bracket.

meanings.s: input string of brackets to validate
meanings.stack: LIFO stack holding open brackets awaiting a match
meanings.map: lookup from each closing bracket to its matching open bracket

title: Merge sorted linked list
why: Link the smaller current head into the result; everything already merged remains sorted.

title: Generate Parentheses
why: An opening bracket may be added while capacity remains; a closing bracket needs an unmatched opening bracket.

meanings.n: Number of pairs of parentheses to generate.
meanings.stack: Explicit char stack holding the current partial string; push on each choice, pop to backtrack.
meanings.open: Count of `(` placed so far on the current path.
meanings.close: Count of `)` placed so far on the current path.
meanings.res: Result list collecting every completed valid combination (`stack.join("")`).

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
why: Each merge combines sorted streams while preserving the order within each original list.

meanings.lists: array of the k sorted linked lists being merged
meanings.l1: first list of the current pair passed to `mergeTwo`
meanings.l2: second list of the current pair (or `null` when odd one out)
meanings.dummy: sentinel head node used while merging a pair
meanings.curr: tail pointer of the merged list being built in `mergeTwo`
meanings.merged: array collecting the merged pair results for the current round

title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
why: Reverse a group only after confirming that all k nodes exist; reconnect both boundaries afterward.

meanings.head: head node of the input linked list
meanings.dummy: sentinel node placed before `head` so the first group has a stable predecessor
meanings.groupPrev: node just before the group currently being reversed
meanings.groupNext: node just after the group (the boundary where reversal stops)
meanings.kth: the k-th node of the current group (its new head after reversal)
meanings.prev: previous node during the in-group reversal
meanings.curr: current node during the in-group reversal
meanings.k: group size to reverse

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
why: The write pointer separates the unique prefix from unread values; the sorted order makes duplicates adjacent.

meanings.nums: sorted input array, deduplicated in place
meanings.left: last unique index / write boundary (the prefix nums[0..left] is unique)
meanings.right: scanner index that walks forward looking for new values
meanings.k: count of unique elements returned, equals left + 1

title: Remove Element
why: Copy each retained value into the next output position; values beyond the returned length are irrelevant.

meanings.nums: input array (mutated in place)
meanings.i: fast / read pointer scanning every element
meanings.k: slow / write pointer; also the count of kept elements
meanings.ans: returned value: final k

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
why: At least one side of the midpoint is sorted. Check whether the target lies in that side before discarding it.

meanings.nums: The rotated sorted input array to search.
meanings.target: The value we are searching for.
meanings.left: Left boundary index of the current search window.
meanings.right: Right boundary index of the current search window.
meanings.mid: Middle index, `Math.floor((left + right) / 2)`; one half around it is always sorted.

title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
why: Equal values form one contiguous run in a sorted array. Lower and upper bounds isolate that run without scanning its duplicates.

meanings.nums: sorted input array with duplicates allowed
meanings.target: value whose range is sought
meanings.left: included left search bound
meanings.right: excluded right search bound; n is a legal sentinel
meanings.mid: middle index in the current nonempty window
meanings.first: first index with a value at least target
meanings.afterLast: first index with a value greater than target
meanings.ans: inclusive first and last indices, or [-1, -1]

title: Search Insert Position
why: The insertion position is the first place whose value is not smaller than the target.

meanings.nums: sorted input array
meanings.target: value to insert
meanings.left: left search bound
meanings.right: right search bound
meanings.ans: insert position

title: Valid Sudoku
why: A digit must be unique independently within its row, column, and three-by-three box.

meanings.board: 9×9 grid of digit chars and '.' for empty
meanings.rows: array of 9 Sets, one per row
meanings.cols: array of 9 Sets, one per column
meanings.boxes: array of 9 Sets, one per 3×3 box
meanings.ans: boolean result: true if valid, false on first conflict

title: Combination Sum
why: Reusing a candidate keeps the search on that candidate; the remaining target measures what is still needed.

meanings.candidates: array of distinct positive numbers we may reuse
meanings.target: sum each combination must reach
meanings.res: output list of all valid combinations
meanings.start: first index this dfs frame may choose from
meanings.remain: target minus the sum of `path` so far
meanings.i: loop index over `candidates`, from `start`

title: Combination Sum II
why: Each input position is used at most once; skipping equal choices at the same depth prevents duplicate combinations.

meanings.candidates: array sorted ascending; each value used at most once
meanings.target: sum each combination must reach
meanings.res: output list of all unique combinations
meanings.start: first index this dfs frame may choose from
meanings.remain: target minus the sum of `path` so far
meanings.i: loop index over `candidates`, from `start`

title: First Missing Positive
why: A positive value x belongs at index x−1. The first position that cannot be filled identifies the missing positive.

meanings.nums: input array (mutated in place)
meanings.n: nums.length
meanings.i: primary loop index (both phases)
meanings.j: target/home index for the value being placed = nums[i] − 1
meanings.ans: return value: first missing positive

title: Trapping Rain Water
why: Water above a position is limited by the smaller of the strongest left and right boundaries.

meanings.left: left pointer
meanings.right: right pointer
meanings.leftMax: tallest bar seen so far from the left
meanings.rightMax: tallest bar seen so far from the right
meanings.res: total trapped water accumulated

title: Multiply Strings
why: Multiplying two digits contributes to a fixed result column; carrying transfers excess into the neighboring column.

meanings.pos: Digit accumulator of length `m + n`; `pos[k]` holds the digit at place `k` (most significant on the left).
meanings.mul: Product of the two current single digits `num1[i] * num2[j]`.
meanings.sum: `mul + pos[p2]` — the new value at the low slot before splitting into digit + carry.
meanings.res: `pos` joined into a string, then with leading zeros stripped.

title: Jump Game II
why: One jump covers a whole reachable range. The farthest reach of that range defines the next jump's boundary.

meanings.nums: Input array; `nums[i]` is the max jump length from index `i`.
meanings.jumps: Count of jumps taken so far; the final answer (minimum jumps to reach the last index).
meanings.curEnd: The farthest index reachable using the current number of jumps — the right edge of the current BFS "level" window.
meanings.farthest: The farthest index reachable from any cell scanned so far; becomes the next `curEnd` when a jump is taken.
meanings.i: Loop pointer scanning indices `0 .. nums.length - 2`.

title: Permutations
why: Choose an unused value, explore the remaining positions, then undo the choice before trying another branch.

meanings.nums: input array of distinct numbers to permute
meanings.res: output list of all complete permutations
meanings.used: boolean flag per index marking which numbers are already in `path`
meanings.i: loop index over `nums` at the current depth

title: Permutations II
why: Equal values must not create equivalent branches at the same decision depth.

meanings.nums: input array (sorted first) that may contain duplicates
meanings.res: output list of all distinct permutations
meanings.used: boolean flag per index marking which numbers are already in `path`
meanings.i: loop index over `nums`; the duplicate guard compares `nums[i]` with `nums[i-1]`

title: Rotate Image
why: A quarter turn moves each cell to its rotated coordinates while preserving every original value.

meanings.matrix: The input `n x n` matrix, rotated 90° clockwise in place.
meanings.n: The side length of the square matrix (`matrix.length`).
meanings.i: Row index. In phase 1 it is the outer transpose index; in phase 2 it selects the row to reverse.
meanings.j: Column index in phase 1, starting at `i + 1` so each pair across the diagonal is swapped exactly once.
meanings.temp: Temporary holder used to swap `matrix[i][j]` with `matrix[j][i]` during the transpose.

title: Group Anagrams
why: Words with the same letter-frequency signature belong in the same group regardless of letter order.

meanings.groups: map from frequency key → word group
meanings.res: array of grouped words

title: Pow(x, n)
why: Squaring the base and halving the exponent reduces the remaining work; an odd exponent contributes one extra base.

meanings.x: The base. When `n` is negative it is replaced by its reciprocal `1 / x`, then repeatedly squared each iteration
meanings.n: The exponent. Made positive up front if negative, then halved (`Math.floor(n / 2)`) until it reaches 0
meanings.res: The accumulator, starting at 1. Whenever the current `n` is odd (`n % 2 === 1`) the current `x` is multiplied into it; returned at the end

title: N-Queens
why: Place one queen per row while excluding occupied columns and diagonals; undo those exclusions on return.

meanings.n: board size (n x n) and number of queens to place
meanings.res: output array of solution boards
meanings.board: current n x n grid of `'.'` / `'Q'`
meanings.cols: Set of columns already occupied by a queen
meanings.diag: Set of occupied `r - c` (top-left to bottom-right) diagonals
meanings.antiDiag: Set of occupied `r + c` (top-right to bottom-left) diagonals
meanings.c: column being tried in the current row

title: N-Queens II
why: A complete conflict-free placement adds one solution; backtracking restores the board for the next placement.

meanings.n: board size (n x n) and number of queens to place
meanings.count: running counter of valid full placements (the answer)
meanings.cols: Set of columns already occupied by a queen
meanings.diag: Set of occupied `r - c` (top-left to bottom-right) diagonals
meanings.antiDiag: Set of occupied `r + c` (top-right to bottom-left) diagonals
meanings.c: column being tried in the current row

title: Maximum Subarray
why: Either extend the previous subarray or start at the current value; keep the best sum seen anywhere.

meanings.nums: The input integer array being scanned.
meanings.curSum: Largest subarray sum that **ends** at the current index `i`. Either extends the previous run (`curSum + nums[i]`) or restarts at `nums[i]`.
meanings.maxSum: Largest subarray sum seen **anywhere** so far; the eventual answer.
meanings.i: Loop index, scanning left to right from `1`.
meanings.ans: The returned value — equals `maxSum` when the loop finishes.

title: Spiral Matrix
why: After traversing one boundary, shrink it so that already visited cells are not visited again.

meanings.matrix: The input 2D matrix to read in spiral order.
meanings.res: The output array collecting cell values in spiral order.
meanings.top: Index of the topmost unvisited row. Increases after the top row is consumed.
meanings.bottom: Index of the bottommost unvisited row. Decreases after the bottom row is consumed.
meanings.left: Index of the leftmost unvisited column. Increases after the left column is consumed.
meanings.right: Index of the rightmost unvisited column. Decreases after the right column is consumed.
meanings.i: Row index used when walking the right column (top→bottom) and the left column (bottom→top).
meanings.j: Column index used when walking the top row (left→right) and the bottom row (right→left).

title: Jump Game
why: A position is usable only if it is within the farthest reach established by earlier positions.

meanings.nums: Input array; `nums[i]` is the max jump length from index `i`.
meanings.goal: The leftmost index currently known to reach the last cell; starts at `nums.length - 1` and shrinks left.
meanings.i: Loop pointer scanning the array from right to left (`nums.length - 2` down to `0`).
meanings.ans: Final boolean: `true` iff `goal` reaches `0`, meaning the start can chain to the end.

title: Merge Intervals
why: Sorted overlapping intervals belong to the same merged interval; a gap starts a new output interval.

meanings.intervals: The input list, sorted in place by start (`a[0] - b[0]`) so overlapping intervals become adjacent.
meanings.res: The merged output list; seeded with the first interval, then extended or appended as the sweep proceeds.
meanings.i: Index sweeping left to right through the sorted `intervals`, starting at 1.
meanings.last: `res[res.length - 1]`, the most recent merged interval — extended when the current bar overlaps it (`start <= last.end`).

title: Insert Interval
why: Keep intervals before the insertion, merge its overlaps, then append the intervals that follow it.

meanings.intervals: The input list of non-overlapping intervals, already sorted by start.
meanings.newInterval: The interval to insert; it grows in Phase 2 as overlapping intervals are absorbed (`[min(start), max(end)]`).
meanings.res: The output list of intervals being assembled across the three phases.
meanings.i: Index sweeping left to right through `intervals`.
meanings.n: `intervals.length`, the fixed loop bound.

title: Unique Paths
why: Every path into a cell arrives from above or from the left, so its count is their sum.

meanings.m: Number of rows in the grid
meanings.n: Number of columns in the grid
meanings.dp: `dp[i][j]` = number of unique paths from the top-left corner to cell `(i, j)`
meanings.i: Current row index in the outer loop
meanings.j: Current column index in the inner loop

title: Unique Paths II
why: An obstacle contributes no paths; other cells combine the reachable counts above and to the left.

meanings.grid: Input grid where `1` marks an obstacle and `0` is an open cell
meanings.m: Number of rows in the grid
meanings.n: Number of columns in the grid
meanings.dp: `dp[i][j]` = number of obstacle-free paths from `(0, 0)` to cell `(i, j)`
meanings.i: Current row index in the outer loop
meanings.j: Current column index in the inner loop

title: Minimum Path Sum
why: Choose the cheaper reachable predecessor, then add the current cell's cost.

meanings.grid: Input grid of non-negative costs for each cell
meanings.m: Number of rows in the grid
meanings.n: Number of columns in the grid
meanings.dp: `dp[i][j]` = minimum total cost to reach cell `(i, j)` moving only right or down
meanings.i: Current row index in the outer loop
meanings.j: Current column index in the inner loop

title: Plus One
why: A digit below nine absorbs the carry; a nine becomes zero and passes the carry left.

meanings.digits: The array of single digits representing one big number, most-significant first. We add 1 to it in place.
meanings.i: The loop index, walking from the rightmost digit (`digits.length - 1`) toward index 0 as the carry propagates.
meanings.carry: Conceptual flag: a digit was 9, so it became 0 and the +1 must continue into the digit to its left.
meanings.ans: The returned array — either the in-place modified `digits`, or `[1, ...digits]` when every digit carried (e.g. `[9,9]` → `[1,0,0]`).

title: Add Binary
why: The two input bits and incoming carry determine the output bit and the next carry.

meanings.res: Result binary string, built one bit at a time by prepending each column's output bit.
meanings.i: Index into `a`, walking from the last character toward index 0.
meanings.j: Index into `b`, walking from the last character toward index 0.
meanings.carry: Carry bit (0 or 1) flowing from the current column into the next column to the left.
meanings.sum: Per-column total = `carry` + current bit of `a` + current bit of `b`; the output bit is `sum % 2`, the new carry is `floor(sum / 2)`.

title: Sqrt(x)
why: Compare a candidate square with x to narrow the range containing the integer square root.

meanings.x: The non-negative integer whose integer square root (floor) we want
meanings.left: Lower bound of the candidate range (starts at 0)
meanings.right: Upper bound of the candidate range (starts at x)
meanings.ans: Largest candidate found so far whose square is `<= x`; the final answer

title: Climbing Stairs
why: The final move climbs one or two stairs, so the number of ways comes from the previous two steps.

meanings.n: The number of stairs to climb to reach the top.
meanings.dp: Array of length `n + 1` where `dp[i]` is the number of distinct ways to reach step `i`. Base cases `dp[0] = 1` and `dp[1] = 1`.
meanings.i: Loop index, from `2` to `n`, marking the step whose count is currently being computed via `dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2]`.

title: Simplify Path
why: A normal directory pushes onto the path stack; two dots pop one directory when possible.

meanings.path: The raw unix-style absolute path string to canonicalize.
meanings.parts: The path split on `"/"`; each segment is a name, `""`, `"."`, or `".."`.
meanings.stack: Directory stack: push a name, pop on `".."`, skip `""` and `"."`; final path is `"/" + stack.join("/")`.

title: Edit Distance
why: Matching characters reuse the diagonal result; a mismatch chooses the cheapest insert, delete, or replace.

meanings.word1: The source string we are editing; its characters label the rows (row `i` ↔ `word1[i-1]`).
meanings.word2: The target string we want to reach; its characters label the columns (col `j` ↔ `word2[j-1]`).
meanings.m: Length of `word1` (number of data rows below the empty-string row).
meanings.n: Length of `word2` (number of data columns after the empty-string column).
meanings.dp: `(m+1)×(n+1)` table where `dp[i][j]` = minimum edits to turn `word1[0..i)` into `word2[0..j)`. Column 0 = `i` (delete all), row 0 = `j` (insert all).
meanings.i: Current row index (`1..m`); selects character `word1[i-1]`.
meanings.j: Current column index (`1..n`); selects character `word2[j-1]`.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
why: Remember which rows and columns originally contain zero before applying those markers to other cells.

meanings.matrix: The input grid, modified in place and returned at the end
meanings.n: Number of columns (`matrix[0].length`)
meanings.rows: Set of row indices that contained at least one zero (filled during pass 1)
meanings.cols: Set of column indices that contained at least one zero (filled during pass 1)
meanings.i: Outer loop index over rows in both the scan pass and the apply pass
meanings.j: Inner loop index over columns in both the scan pass and the apply pass

title: Search a 2D Matrix
why: Sorted row boundaries let the matrix act like one sorted sequence with row/column coordinates.

meanings.matrix: The row-sorted 2D grid; row-major order makes it one sorted sequence
meanings.target: The value we are searching for
meanings.n: Number of columns, `matrix[0].length`
meanings.left: Lower bound of the virtual 1-D index range (starts at 0)
meanings.right: Upper bound of the virtual 1-D index range (starts at m*n - 1)
meanings.mid: Current virtual index; the cell is `matrix[Math.floor(mid / n)][mid % n]`

title: Sort Colors
why: Maintain regions for zeros, ones, unknown values, and twos; each swap shrinks the unknown region.

meanings.nums: input array containing only 0s, 1s, and 2s (sorted in-place)
meanings.low: boundary of the 0-region; everything in [0..low-1] is 0
meanings.mid: scanning pointer; nums[mid] is the value currently examined
meanings.high: boundary of the 2-region; everything in [high+1..] is 2

title: Minimum Window Substring
why: Grow until all required character counts are covered, then shrink while preserving that coverage.

meanings.s: source string to search within
meanings.t: target string whose characters must all be covered
meanings.need: frequency map of the characters in t
meanings.window: frequency map of the characters currently in [left, right]
meanings.left: left bound of the current window
meanings.right: right bound of the current window
meanings.have: number of distinct chars whose required count is currently met
meanings.ans: smallest valid window substring found so far

title: Combinations
why: Each selected number moves the next starting position forward, producing combinations without reordering duplicates.

meanings.n: numbers to choose from are `1..n`
meanings.k: size each combination must reach
meanings.res: output list of all combinations
meanings.start: smallest number this dfs frame may choose
meanings.i: loop variable iterating `start..n`

title: Subsets
why: Each input value creates an include branch and an exclude branch; complete decisions produce the subsets.

meanings.nums: input array of distinct numbers
meanings.res: output list collecting every subset
meanings.i: index of the element this dfs frame decides (take or skip)

title: Word Search
why: Follow adjacent matching cells without reusing a cell in the current path; restore it when that path returns.

meanings.word: the word we are trying to spell
meanings.i: index of the letter in `word` we need next

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
why: Duplicate boundary values can hide the sorted side; remove ambiguity before choosing a search half.

meanings.nums: The rotated sorted input array, which may contain duplicates.
meanings.target: The value we are searching for.
meanings.left: Left boundary index of the current search window.
meanings.right: Right boundary index of the current search window.
meanings.mid: Middle index, `Math.floor((left + right) / 2)`; when `nums[left] === nums[mid] === nums[right]` the sorted half is ambiguous and both ends shrink.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
why: Popping a taller bar establishes its right boundary; the remaining stack establishes its left boundary.

meanings.dirs: The four movement deltas `[[1,0],[-1,0],[0,1],[0,-1]]` (down, up, right, left).

title: House Robber II
why: The first and last houses are neighbors, so compare solutions excluding one endpoint at a time.

meanings.nums: Money in each house, arranged in a **circle** (house `0` and house `n-1` are adjacent).
meanings.n: Number of houses, `nums.length`.
meanings.robLine: Helper that solves the **linear** House Robber on a sub-array via a rolling DP.
meanings.prev: Best loot using houses up to two positions back (the `dp[i-2]` role).
meanings.curr: Best loot using houses up to the previous position (the `dp[i-1]` role); ends as the slice answer.
meanings.next: Candidate best for the current house: `max(curr, prev + x)` — skip it or rob it.
meanings.x: Current house value being considered inside `robLine`.
meanings.ans: Final answer: `max(robLine(exclude last), robLine(exclude first))`.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
why: Keeping only k large candidates makes the smallest retained value the kth largest.

meanings.nums: input array of numbers
meanings.k: which largest element to return (the kth largest)
meanings.heap: a MinHeap capped at size k, holding the k largest values seen so far
meanings.num: the current number from `nums` being pushed onto the heap

title: Contains Duplicate
why: A value already present in the seen set proves a duplicate; otherwise remember it for later comparisons.

meanings.nums: input array
meanings.i: current index

title: Contains Duplicate II
why: Keep only values within k previous positions; a matching value in that window satisfies the distance constraint.

meanings.nums: input array of numbers
meanings.k: maximum allowed distance between two equal values
meanings.i: loop index; the right edge of the sliding window
meanings.seen: Set of the values currently inside the window `[i-k, i]`
meanings.ans: boolean answer: `true` if a duplicate exists within distance `k`, else `false`

title: Implement Stack using Queues
why: Queue rotations place the newest value where a stack pop can remove it first.

meanings.q: the single backing FIFO queue; `q[0]` is the front (the logical top of the stack)
meanings.i: loop index used while rotating the queue so the newest element reaches the front

title: Invert Binary Tree
why: Swapping each node's children mirrors the entire tree when applied throughout the structure.

meanings.root: tree root node passed into `invertTree`
meanings.node: current node in the recursion (its `left`/`right` get swapped)
meanings.ans: final answer: the inverted tree (shown as a level-order array)

title: Majority Element II
why: At most two values can occur more than one-third of the time; verify the surviving candidates after cancellation.

meanings.nums: input array
meanings.num: current value being read in each pass
meanings.count1: vote counter for cand1 (reused as a true recount in the verification pass)
meanings.count2: vote counter for cand2 (reused as a true recount in the verification pass)
meanings.res: output array of values appearing more than ⌊n/3⌋ times

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
why: Inorder visits a BST in sorted order, so the kth visit identifies the kth smallest value.

meanings.root: root of the binary search tree
meanings.k: which smallest value to find; decremented on each inorder visit until it reaches 0
meanings.stack: explicit stack holding the path of nodes whose left subtree is being processed
meanings.node: current node; walks left while pushing, then is set to each popped node, then to its right child

title: Implement Queue using Stacks
why: Transferring values between two stacks reverses their order so the oldest value leaves first.

meanings.sIn: input stack; every `push` lands here (newest on top)
meanings.sOut: output stack; serves the oldest element. Filled by pouring `sIn` into it, which reverses the order so the oldest element ends up on top

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
why: If both targets lie on one side, descend there; their first split identifies the common ancestor.

meanings.root: root node of the BST
meanings.node: current node on the search path
meanings.ans: the lowest common ancestor returned

title: Product of Array Except Self
why: Multiply the values before and after each position without including that position itself.

meanings.nums: input array
meanings.res: output array
meanings.i: current index

title: Sliding Window Maximum
why: Remove weaker candidates from the deque's back and expired indices from its front; the front is the maximum.

meanings.nums: input array of numbers
meanings.k: window size
meanings.deque: indices whose values stay strictly decreasing from front to back; the front is the current window max
meanings.left: left bound of the current window (right - k + 1)
meanings.right: right bound of the current window (driven by the for loop)
meanings.res: output array of each window's maximum

title: Valid Anagram
why: Equal letter counts characterize anagrams even when the letters appear in different orders.

meanings.s: first string
meanings.i: current index

title: Meeting Rooms
why: After sorting meetings, a start before the previous end exposes an overlap.

meanings.intervals: Array of `[start, end]` meeting times, sorted ascending by start time
meanings.i: Loop index (starts at 1); compares meeting `i` against the previous meeting `i - 1`
meanings.intervals[i][0]: Start time of the current meeting
meanings.intervals[i - 1][1]: End time of the previous meeting
meanings.ans: Boolean result — `true` if the person can attend every meeting, `false` if any two overlap

title: Meeting Rooms II
why: A room becomes reusable when its meeting ends; overlapping active meetings require separate rooms.

meanings.starts: All meeting start times, sorted ascending — the "rising" events of the sweep line
meanings.ends: All meeting end times, sorted ascending — the "falling" events of the sweep line
meanings.rooms: Number of meetings currently in progress; `++` on a start event, `--` on an end event
meanings.maxRooms: Running maximum of `rooms` — the peak concurrency, i.e. the minimum rooms needed (returned)
meanings.s: Pointer into `starts` — index of the next meeting to begin
meanings.e: Pointer into `ends` — index of the next meeting to finish

title: Graph Valid Tree
why: A tree must connect every node while introducing no cycle.

meanings.n: Number of nodes, labeled `0..n-1`. A tree on `n` nodes has exactly `n-1` edges.
meanings.edges: Undirected edges `[a, b]`. The graph is a tree iff it has `n-1` edges and no cycle.
meanings.dsu: The `DSU` (union-find) instance used to detect a cycle while joining edges.
meanings.parent: `parent[x]` is `x`'s parent pointer; following it to a fixed point gives the set's root.
meanings.a: First endpoint of the current edge.
meanings.b: Second endpoint of the current edge.
meanings.rb: `find(b)` — the root of `b`'s set. If `ra === rb`, the edge forms a cycle.
meanings.ans: Boolean result: `true` only if the edge-count gate passes and every `union` succeeds (no cycle).

title: Missing Number
why: Compare the complete range with the supplied values to isolate the one missing number.

meanings.nums: Distinct integers, a permutation of `0..n` with exactly one missing
meanings.res: XOR accumulator; starts at `n`, then XORs every index and value so matched pairs cancel
meanings.i: Loop index; both `i` and `nums[i]` are XOR-ed into `res`

title: Alien Dictionary
why: The first differing characters of adjacent words establish an ordering edge; cycles make the ordering impossible.

meanings.words: The list of alien words, already sorted in the unknown alphabet's lexicographic order. The whole problem is to recover that order.
meanings.adj: `Map<char, Set<char>>` adjacency list. `adj[a]` holds every character that must come *after* `a`. An edge `a → b` means `a` precedes `b`.
meanings.indegree: `Map<char, number>` counting how many edges point *into* each character. A character with indegree 0 has no unresolved predecessor and may be emitted next. Its `.size` is the number of distinct characters.
meanings.w1: The earlier word of the adjacent pair `words[i]` being compared.
meanings.w2: The later word of the adjacent pair `words[i + 1]`. The first position where `w1` and `w2` differ reveals one ordering constraint.
meanings.minLen: `Math.min(w1.length, w2.length)` — only the shared-length prefix can be compared. If `w1` is longer but the prefix is identical (`["abc","ab"]`), the input is invalid and the answer is `""`.
meanings.queue: The Kahn (BFS) queue, seeded with every indegree-0 character. Processed with a moving `head` index instead of `shift()`, so it doubles as the visit history.
meanings.res: The result string built one character at a time as nodes are popped. If `res.length` ends up less than `indegree.size`, a cycle exists (e.g. `["z","x","z"]`) and the function returns `""`.
meanings.ch: The character currently popped from the queue (and appended to `res`), or the loop variable while registering nodes.
meanings.nei: A neighbor of `ch` (`ch → nei`). Its indegree is decremented; if it drops to 0 it is enqueued.

title: Encode and Decode Strings
why: A length prefix specifies exactly how many characters belong to the next string, including separator characters.

meanings.i: read pointer in encoded string

title: Perfect Squares
why: Try a final square and reuse the best solution for the remaining amount.

meanings.n: The target value. We want the fewest perfect squares (1, 4, 9, 16, …) that sum to it.
meanings.dp: `dp[k]` = the minimum number of perfect squares that sum to `k`. Length `n + 1`, filled with `Infinity` except `dp[0] = 0`.
meanings.i: The outer-loop value currently being solved, from `1` to `n`.
meanings.j: The inner-loop counter producing the candidate square `j * j` (bounded by `j * j <= i`). It reads `dp[i - j*j]` and proposes `dp[i - j*j] + 1`.

title: Walls and Gates
why: Starting breadth-first search at every gate finds each room's nearest gate in expanding distance layers.

meanings.rooms: The `rows x cols` grid; mutated in place so each empty room holds its distance to the nearest gate.
meanings.INF: The empty-room sentinel `2147483647`; a cell is fillable only while it still equals `INF`.
meanings.queue: The BFS frontier of `[r, c]` cells for the current level; reassigned to `next` after each level (level-by-level multi-source BFS).
meanings.nr: Neighbor row `r + dr` being considered for filling.
meanings.nc: Neighbor column `c + dc` being considered for filling.

title: Find the Duplicate Number
why: Treat values as next indices; the repeated value creates a cycle whose entrance is the duplicate.

meanings.nums: input array of n+1 integers, each in the range 1..n-1, treated as an implicit linked list where index `i` links to index `nums[i]`
meanings.slow: slow pointer; advances one step per move (`slow = nums[slow]`)
meanings.fast: fast pointer; advances two steps per move (`fast = nums[nums[fast]]`), then one step per move in phase 2

title: Find Median from Data Stream
why: Two balanced heaps separate the lower and upper halves, exposing the middle value or pair.

meanings.small: Max-heap holding the lower half of the stream; its root is the largest of the small numbers.
meanings.large: Min-heap holding the upper half of the stream; its root is the smallest of the large numbers.
meanings.num: The value passed to `addNum`; pushed into `small` first, then rebalanced across the two heaps.
meanings.median: Top of the larger heap when sizes differ; the average of the two roots when sizes are equal.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
why: Record missing children as well as values so deserialization can reconstruct the original tree shape.

meanings.root: root of the tree being serialized (and the tree rebuilt by deserialize)
meanings.res: array collected during serialize: each `node.val` plus a `"null"` marker for every missing child
meanings.node: current node during the preorder DFS of each phase
meanings.data: the comma-joined serialized string passed from serialize to deserialize
meanings.vals: `data.split(",")`, the token list consumed during deserialize
meanings.i: index into `vals`; advances left-to-right as deserialize rebuilds the tree

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
why: An increasing subsequence can extend only through a larger value; retain the best length reachable at each choice.

meanings.nums: Input integer array.
meanings.n: Number of elements, `nums.length`.
meanings.dp: `dp[i]` = length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence that **ends** at index `i`; initialized to all `1`.
meanings.ans: Best value seen across the whole `dp` array — the LIS length to return.
meanings.i: Outer-loop index (the element whose `dp[i]` we are computing).
meanings.j: Inner-loop index over earlier elements; if `nums[j] < nums[i]`, element `j` can extend a subsequence into `i`.

title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
why: Combine prefix rectangles with inclusion-exclusion to count every cell in the query exactly once.

meanings.matrix: input m × n grid of numbers
meanings.prefix: (m+1) × (n+1) prefix-sum matrix; prefix[i][j] = sum of all source cells above and left of (i, j)
meanings.row1: top row of the query rectangle
meanings.col1: left column of the query rectangle
meanings.row2: bottom row of the query rectangle
meanings.col2: right column of the query rectangle

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
why: The cooldown constrains transitions between holding, selling, and resting states.

meanings.prices: Input array of daily stock prices
meanings.n: Number of days (length of `prices`)
meanings.hold: `hold[i]` = max profit on day `i` while **owning** a share
meanings.sold: `sold[i]` = max profit on day `i` if you **sold today** (next day is a forced cooldown)
meanings.rest: `rest[i]` = max profit on day `i` while **idle** (not holding, free to buy)
meanings.i: Current day index in the loop
meanings.ans: Final answer = `max(sold[n-1], rest[n-1])` (never end while still holding)

title: Minimum Height Trees
why: Removing leaves in layers reveals the center or two centers that minimize tree height.

meanings.n: Number of nodes labeled `0..n-1`. The tree has exactly `n - 1` edges. `n === 1` returns `[0]`.
meanings.edges: Undirected edges `[a, b]`; each adds `b` to `adj[a]` and `a` to `adj[b]`.
meanings.adj: Adjacency list; `adj[v]` is the list of `v`'s neighbors.
meanings.degree: `degree[v]` = current number of remaining neighbors of `v`. A node is a leaf when `degree === 1`.
meanings.leaves: The current outer layer (all nodes with `degree === 1`) being trimmed this round.
meanings.remaining: Count of nodes not yet peeled; the loop runs while `remaining > 2`.
meanings.nei: A neighbor of a leaf being removed; its `degree` is decremented, and it joins the next layer if it becomes a leaf.
meanings.ans: The returned value: the 1 or 2 surviving centroid nodes — the roots of all minimum-height trees.

title: Burst Balloons
why: Choosing the last balloon in an interval makes its two remaining neighbors known and splits the other work.

meanings.nums: Input array of balloon values.
meanings.balloons: Padded array `[1, ...nums, 1]` so the boundaries always multiply by 1.
meanings.n: Length of the padded `balloons` array.
meanings.dp: Upper-triangular table; `dp[left][right]` = max coins from bursting every balloon strictly between the open boundaries `left` and `right`.
meanings.left: Left open boundary of the current interval (not burst).
meanings.right: Right open boundary, `right = left + len`.
meanings.k: The **last** balloon burst inside `(left, right)`; scanned `left+1 .. right-1`.
meanings.len: Current interval span (outer loop runs `2..n-1`); the table fills by increasing length.
meanings.ans: Final answer `dp[0][n-1]`.

title: Coin Change
why: Each candidate coin extends a solution for a smaller amount; keep the fewest coins among reachable choices.

meanings.coins: The available coin denominations. Each coin can be used unlimited times (unbounded knapsack).
meanings.amount: The target total we want to make with the fewest coins.
meanings.dp: `dp[k]` = the minimum number of coins that sum to amount `k`. Length `amount + 1`, filled with `Infinity` (unreachable) except `dp[0] = 0`.
meanings.a: The outer-loop amount currently being solved, from `1` to `amount`.
meanings.coin: The inner-loop candidate coin. Only usable when `coin <= a`; it reads `dp[a - coin]` and proposes `dp[a - coin] + 1`.
meanings.ans: The result: `dp[amount]`, or `-1` if it is still `Infinity` (the amount cannot be formed).

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
why: Connecting two previously separate components reduces the component count by one.

meanings.n: Number of nodes, labeled `0..n-1`.
meanings.edges: Undirected edges `[a, b]`; each may or may not connect two separate components.
meanings.dsu: The `DSU` (union-find) instance; its `count` field tracks the live component total.
meanings.parent: `parent[x]` is `x`'s parent pointer; following it to a fixed point yields the component root.
meanings.count: Number of connected components. Starts at `n`, and `count--` each time `union` joins two different sets. This is the answer.
meanings.a: First endpoint of the current edge.
meanings.b: Second endpoint of the current edge.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
why: A move must increase the cell value, so each cell can reuse the longest increasing continuation from its neighbors.

meanings.rows: Number of rows in the matrix
meanings.cols: Number of columns in the matrix
meanings.memo: `memo[r][c]` = length of the longest strictly-increasing path that starts at cell `(r, c)` (0 = not computed yet)
meanings.dirs: The four step directions: up, down, left, right
meanings.dfs: Recursive helper that returns the longest increasing path starting at `(r, c)`, caching the result in `memo`
meanings.r: Row index of the cell currently being explored
meanings.c: Column index of the cell currently being explored
meanings.nr: Row index of a neighbor being probed (`r + dr`)
meanings.nc: Column index of a neighbor being probed (`c + dc`)
meanings.best: Longest path found so far starting at `(r, c)`; at least 1 (the cell itself)
meanings.ans: Overall answer = the longest increasing path anywhere in the matrix

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
why: Consume tickets while constructing a route that uses every edge; lexical choices resolve valid alternatives.

meanings.tickets: List of `[from, to]` airport pairs. Each ticket is a directed edge that must be used **exactly once**.
meanings.adj: `Map` from an airport to its list of destinations. Built from `tickets`, then each list is sorted lexically.
meanings.dests: The destination list `adj.get(airport)` for the airport currently being visited. `shift()` removes (consumes) the smallest unused edge.
meanings.res: The route collected in **post-order** — an airport is pushed only after all of its outgoing edges are used. Reversed at the end to give the itinerary.
meanings.visit: Recursive Hierholzer DFS. Drains an airport's edges, recursing greedily into the lexically smallest first.
meanings.airport: The airport whose frame is currently on the call stack (argument to `visit`).
meanings.next: The destination just `shift()`-ed off `dests`; the recursion target `visit(next)`.
meanings.from: Origin airport of a ticket while building `adj`.
meanings.to: Destination airport of a ticket while building `adj`.

title: House Robber III
why: Robbing a node excludes its children; skipping it allows the better choice independently in each child subtree.

meanings.root: root node of the binary tree
meanings.node: current node in the `dfs` recursion
meanings.left: pair `[robThis, skipThis]` returned by the left child
meanings.right: pair `[robThis, skipThis]` returned by the right child
meanings.withRoot: best total if we rob this node: `node.val + left[1] + right[1]`
meanings.withoutRoot: best total if we skip this node: `max(left) + max(right)`
meanings.res: pair `[withRoot, withoutRoot]` returned by `dfs(root)`

title: Counting Bits
why: Removing or shifting a known bit links the current bit count to an already computed smaller value.

meanings.n: Upper bound; we count set bits for every value `0..n`
meanings.dp: Result array; `dp[i]` is the number of set bits in `i`
meanings.i: Loop index; `dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1)` reuses the answer for `i` with its lowest bit dropped

title: Integer Break
why: Compare every split, allowing each remaining part to stay whole or be split further.

meanings.n: The input integer to break into the sum of at least two positive integers, maximizing their product.
meanings.dp: Array of length `n + 1`; `dp[i]` is the maximum product obtainable by breaking `i` into two or more positive parts. `dp[1] = 1` is the base case.
meanings.i: Outer-loop value 2..n — the number whose best break (`dp[i]`) is currently being computed.
meanings.j: Inner-loop split point 1..i-1. For each `j` we compare `j * (i - j)` (leave `i - j` whole) and `j * dp[i - j]` (break `i - j` further), taking the running max into `dp[i]`.

title: Reverse String
why: Swap the two endpoint characters and move inward until every mirrored pair is settled.

meanings.s: character array being reversed in place
meanings.left: left pointer, starts at index 0
meanings.right: right pointer, starts at index s.length - 1

title: Top K Frequent Element
why: Count occurrences before selecting the k values with the highest frequencies.

meanings.nums: input array
meanings.k: number of most frequent elements to return
meanings.res: top k frequent elements

title: Design Twitter
why: Merge the newest available posts from followed users, taking the next most recent post each time.

meanings.time: Global clock; increments after every `postTweet` so newer tweets get larger timestamps.
meanings.tweets: Map from userId to a list of `[time, tweetId]` entries (that user's timeline).
meanings.following: Map from userId to a Set of the userIds they follow.
meanings.heap: Per-feed max-heap keyed by `entry[0]` (time); merges the followed users' tweets so the newest sits on top.
meanings.res: The news feed: up to the 10 most recent tweet IDs, newest first.

title: Sum of Two Integers
why: XOR adds without carry; shifted AND identifies the carry that still needs to be added.

meanings.a: First integer; also accumulates the running carry-less sum (`a ^ b`). Becomes the final answer.
meanings.b: Second integer; reused each iteration to hold the carry that still needs to be added. Loop ends when `b` is 0.
meanings.carry: The carry bits for this step, computed as `(a & b) << 1`. Columns where both `a` and `b` are 1 produce a carry into the next-higher bit.

title: Guess Number Higher or Lower
why: The feedback eliminates every candidate on one side of the guess.

meanings.n: Upper bound of the guessing range; we search the integers 1..n
meanings.left: Lower bound of the current search range (starts at 1)
meanings.right: Upper bound of the current search range (starts at n)
meanings.pick: The hidden target number; only the `guess()` API can see it
meanings.res: Result of `guess(mid)`: 0 if correct, -1 if mid is too high, 1 if mid is too low

title: Combination Sum IV
why: Choosing the final number extends ordered sequences for a smaller total; different orders count separately.

meanings.nums: The numbers we may use, each an unlimited number of times.
meanings.target: The total we want to reach. We count how many ordered sequences sum to it.
meanings.dp: `dp[k]` = the number of ordered combinations of `nums` that sum to `k`. Length `target + 1`, filled with `0` except `dp[0] = 1` (the empty combination).
meanings.t: The outer-loop running total currently being solved, from `1` to `target`.
meanings.num: The inner-loop candidate treated as the LAST element of the sum. When `num <= t`, it adds `dp[t - num]` ways. Because the outer loop is the total, order matters.
meanings.ans: The result: `dp[target]`, the count of ordered combinations summing to `target`.

title: Decode String
why: A stack preserves the enclosing string and repeat count while a nested bracketed section is decoded.

meanings.s: The encoded input string being scanned left to right.
meanings.stack: LIFO stack of entries `[curStr, curNum]` saved when a `[` opens a group.
meanings.curStr: The string built so far at the current bracket depth.
meanings.curNum: The repeat-count being accumulated from digit characters.

title: Evaluate Division
why: Multiplying edge ratios along a connected path gives the ratio between its endpoints.

meanings.equations: List of variable pairs `[a, b]`; each means the ratio `a / b` is known.
meanings.values: `values[i]` is the numeric value of `equations[i]`, i.e. `a / b`.
meanings.queries: List of `[c, d]` pairs asking for the value of `c / d`.
meanings.graph: A `Map` from each variable to its weighted out-edges `[neighbour, ratio]`.
meanings.addEdge: Helper that appends a directed weighted edge `a -> b` with weight `w`.
meanings.dfs: Recursive search from `src` to `dst`, multiplying edge weights along the path.
meanings.src: The variable the current DFS frame starts from.
meanings.dst: The destination variable the query is trying to reach.
meanings.visited: A `Set` of variables on the current path, preventing cycles.
meanings.w: The weight (ratio) of the edge being traversed out of `src`.
meanings.res: The array of query answers; `-1.0` marks an undefined or unreachable ratio.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
why: A proposed maximum sum determines how many groups are needed; binary search finds the smallest feasible maximum.

meanings.nums: array of non-negative integers to split
meanings.k: number of contiguous subarrays to split into
meanings.left: low end of the candidate largest-sum range (starts at max(nums))
meanings.right: high end of the candidate largest-sum range (starts at sum(nums))
meanings.mid: candidate largest-sum value being tested = floor((left + right) / 2)
meanings.ans: smallest feasible largest-sum found so far (the answer)

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
why: Equal partition is possible exactly when a subset reaches half the total sum.

meanings.nums: The input array of positive integers we try to split into two equal-sum halves.
meanings.total: Sum of every element in `nums`. If it is odd, an equal split is impossible.
meanings.target: `total / 2` — the subset sum each half must reach.
meanings.dp: Boolean array of length `target + 1`; `dp[c]` is `true` when some subset of `nums` sums to capacity `c`. Reused as the 1-D rolling row of the 0/1 knapsack.
meanings.num: The current number from `nums` being considered for inclusion in a subset.
meanings.i: Capacity index, swept **downward** from `target` to `num` so each `num` is used at most once. `dp[i]` becomes `true` whenever `dp[i - num]` is already `true`.
meanings.ans: Final result `dp[target]` — `true` if the array can be partitioned into two equal-sum subsets, else `false`.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
why: Search backward from each ocean along nondecreasing heights; their intersection reaches both oceans.

meanings.heights: The `rows x cols` matrix of cell elevations. Water flows from a cell to an equal-or-lower neighbor.
meanings.pac: Boolean matrix; `pac[r][c]` is `true` once cell `(r,c)` can drain to the Pacific (top/left edges).
meanings.atl: Boolean matrix; `atl[r][c]` is `true` once cell `(r,c)` can drain to the Atlantic (bottom/right edges).
meanings.dfs: Reverse flood-fill `(r, c, ocean, prev)`: from an ocean border, walk **uphill** (only to neighbors `>= prev`) marking every reachable cell in `ocean`.
meanings.prev: The height of the cell we came from; a neighbor is reachable only if its height is `>= prev`.
meanings.res: The answer: every `[r, c]` with `pac[r][c] && atl[r][c]` — cells that drain to **both** oceans.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
why: Window length minus its most frequent character count is the number of replacements needed.

meanings.s: input string
meanings.k: max number of characters allowed to replace
