meanings.j: Inner index walking both words character by character until they differ or one ends.
meanings.w1: The earlier word in the current pair, `words[i]`.
meanings.w2: The later word in the current pair, `words[i + 1]`.
meanings.ans: The returned value: `true` if all adjacent pairs are correctly ordered, else `false` (a bigger-ranked first-difference, or `w2` being a strict prefix of `w1`).

title: K Closest Points to Origin
why: Squared distance preserves distance ordering, so square roots are unnecessary when selecting nearby points.

meanings.k: How many closest points to return.
meanings.heap: Min-heap of `[dist, x, y]` tuples, compared by `el[0]` (squared distance).
meanings.dist: Squared distance `x*x + y*y` of the current point (no `sqrt` needed for ordering).
meanings.res: Result list collecting the `k` popped (closest) points.
meanings.i: Loop counter for the `k` pops.

title: Longest Turbulent Subarray
why: A valid extension flips the comparison direction; equality or a repeated direction starts a new candidate window.

meanings.arr: The input integer array being scanned for a turbulent (zig-zag) run.
meanings.ans: Length of the longest turbulent subarray found so far; starts at `1`.
meanings.inc: Length of the current turbulent run that **ends on an UP step** (`arr[i] > arr[i-1]`).
meanings.dec: Length of the current turbulent run that **ends on a DOWN step** (`arr[i] < arr[i-1]`).
meanings.i: Loop index comparing `arr[i]` against its left neighbour `arr[i-1]`, from `1`.

title: Time Based Key-Value Store
why: For one key, locate the latest timestamp that does not exceed the query time.

meanings.store: A `Map` from each key to an array of `[timestamp, value]` pairs, kept in timestamp order
meanings.left: Left bound of the binary search over the key's timestamp list (inside `get`)
meanings.right: Right bound of the binary search over the key's timestamp list (inside `get`)
meanings.res: The best value found so far whose timestamp is `<=` the query; `""` if none

title: Rotting Oranges
why: Each breadth-first layer spreads rot by one minute; remaining fresh cells after expansion are unreachable.

meanings.grid: The input matrix; `0` empty, `1` fresh orange, `2` rotten orange. BFS flips fresh to rotten.
meanings.queue: Current BFS frontier of rotten cells `[r, c]`; one full sweep of it equals one minute.
meanings.fresh: Count of fresh oranges still left; the loop stops when it reaches `0`.
meanings.minutes: Running answer: BFS levels elapsed. Returned if `fresh === 0`, otherwise `-1`.

title: Find the Town Judge
why: The judge must receive trust from everyone else while trusting nobody.

meanings.n: Number of people, labeled `1..n`. The judge must have a net score of exactly `n - 1`.
meanings.trust: List of directed edges `[a, b]` meaning person `a` trusts person `b`.
meanings.score: Array of length `n + 1`; `score[p]` = (people who trust `p`) − (people `p` trusts). A judge gets `+1` from everyone and never spends a `−1`.
meanings.a: The truster in the current edge `[a, b]`; `score[a]--` (trusting disqualifies you).
meanings.b: The trustee in the current edge `[a, b]`; `score[b]++`.
meanings.i: Loop index over candidates `1..n` while scanning for the judge.
meanings.ans: The returned value: the judge's label if some `score[i] === n - 1`, otherwise `-1`.

title: Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days
why: A proposed capacity determines the required shipping days; search for the smallest capacity meeting the day limit.

meanings.weights: array of package weights, shipped in order
meanings.days: maximum number of days allowed to ship everything
meanings.left: low end of the candidate capacity range (starts at max(weights))
meanings.right: high end of the candidate capacity range (starts at sum(weights))
meanings.mid: candidate ship capacity being tested = floor((left + right) / 2)
meanings.ans: smallest feasible capacity found so far (the answer)

title: Last Stone Weight
why: Remove the two heaviest stones; only their difference returns when their weights are unequal.

meanings.heap: a MaxHeap so the root is always the heaviest stone
meanings.s: the current stone weight being pushed while building the heap
meanings.a: the heaviest stone, popped first each round
meanings.b: the second heaviest stone, popped next

title: Last Stone Weight II
why: Split the stones into sums as close as possible; the smallest leftover is the difference between the groups.

meanings.stones: Input array of positive stone weights to smash together.
meanings.total: Sum of all stone weights; the two final piles must add up to this.
meanings.target: `floor(total / 2)` — the ideal size of the smaller pile; we maximize a subset sum that does not exceed it.
meanings.dp: 1-D array of length `target + 1`; `dp[j]` = the largest achievable subset sum that is `≤ j`.
meanings.stone: The current stone being considered in the outer loop (each stone used at most once).
meanings.j: Inner-loop index sweeping from `target` down to `stone`; the `dp` cell currently being updated.

title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
why: A common repeated base must reproduce both strings; its length divides both string lengths.

meanings.str1: First input string; the answer is taken as a prefix of this string
meanings.str2: Second input string; compared against str1 for a common base unit
meanings.gcd: Recursive Euclid helper `(a, b) => b === 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b)` run on the two lengths
meanings.len: `gcd(str1.length, str2.length)` — the length of the largest common divisor string
meanings.ans: Return value: `str1.substring(0, len)`, or `""` when `str1 + str2 !== str2 + str1`

title: Car Pooling
why: Pickups increase and drop-offs decrease occupancy along the route; capacity must hold after every change.

meanings.trips: Input `[num, start, end]` triples, sorted ascending by `start`.
meanings.capacity: Maximum passengers the car can hold at once.
meanings.heap: Min-heap of `[end, num]` tuples, compared by `el[0]` (drop-off location).
meanings.cur: Passengers currently on board; must never exceed `capacity`.

title: Find in Mountain Array
why: Locate the peak, then search the increasing and decreasing portions using their respective comparison directions.

meanings.arr: The mountain array (strictly increasing, then strictly decreasing)
meanings.target: The value we are searching for
meanings.n: `arr.length`
meanings.left: Left bound of the current search window
meanings.right: Right bound of the current search window
meanings.peak: Index of the mountain's peak (found in phase 1)
meanings.res: Result of the ascending search; the final answer, or `-1`

title: N-th Tribonacci Number
why: Every new term combines the previous three terms; those three dependencies move forward together.

meanings.n: The index of the Tribonacci number to return. Base cases: `T(0) = 0`, `T(1) = 1`, `T(2) = 1`.
meanings.dp: Array of length `n + 1` where `dp[i]` is the i-th Tribonacci number. Built only when `n > 2`; otherwise the function returns the base case directly.
meanings.i: Loop index, from `3` to `n`, marking the term currently being computed via `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2] + dp[i-3]` (the sum of the previous three terms).

title: Stone Game II
why: The state includes both the current position and M, because M determines the next player's allowed choices.

meanings.n: Number of piles, `piles.length`.
meanings.suffix: Suffix-sum array; `suffix[i]` = total stones in `piles[i..n-1]`. Built right-to-left.
meanings.dp: Table indexed by `(i, M)`; `dp[i][M]` = max stones the player to move can secure starting at index `i` when allowed to take `1..2M` piles.
meanings.i: Current starting pile index (outer loop runs `n-1` down to `0`).
meanings.m: Current `M` value (how many piles may be taken is `1..2M`).
meanings.x: Candidate number of piles taken this turn, scanned `1..2M`.
meanings.best: Running maximum over `x` of `suffix[i] - dp[i+x][max(M, x)]`.
meanings.ans: Final answer `dp[0][1]`.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
why: Matching characters extend the diagonal subsequence; a mismatch compares skipping a character from either string.

meanings.text1: First input string; its characters label the rows of the DP table (row `i` ↔ `text1[i-1]`).
meanings.text2: Second input string; its characters label the columns (col `j` ↔ `text2[j-1]`).
meanings.m: Length of `text1` (number of data rows below the empty-string row).
meanings.n: Length of `text2` (number of data columns after the empty-string column).
meanings.dp: `(m+1)×(n+1)` table where `dp[i][j]` = length of the LCS of `text1[0..i)` and `text2[0..j)`. Row 0 / col 0 are all `0` (empty string).
meanings.i: Current row index (`1..m`); selects character `text1[i-1]`.
meanings.j: Current column index (`1..n`); selects character `text2[j-1]`.

title: Delete Leaves With a Given Value
why: Process children before deciding whether their parent has become a removable target-valued leaf.

meanings.root: current node being processed by `removeLeafNodes`
meanings.node: the active node in the recursion (same as `root` inside a frame)
meanings.target: leaf value to delete
meanings.root.left: left child after its subtree has been pruned (may be `null`)
meanings.root.right: right child after its subtree has been pruned (may be `null`)

title: Longest Happy String
why: Choose a frequent character unless it would create three equal consecutive characters; then use an alternative.

meanings.heap: Max-heap of `[count, char]`, compared by `count` (element `[0]`); root is the most plentiful letter.
meanings.res: The happy string being built; never contains `"aaa"`, `"bbb"`, or `"ccc"`.

title: Stone Game III
why: Compare taking one, two, or three stones against the opponent's best remaining score advantage.

meanings.stoneValue: The input row of stone values. Alice and Bob alternate, each taking the first 1, 2, or 3 remaining stones; both play optimally.
meanings.n: Number of stones, `stoneValue.length`.
meanings.dp: Suffix-DP array of length `n + 1`, filled **right → left**. `dp[i]` is the best achievable (current player − opponent) score margin when the game starts at index `i`; `dp[n] = 0` is the empty-suffix base case.
meanings.take: Running sum of the stones the current player grabs (1, 2, or up to 3) at index `i`.
meanings.i: Outer index, decremented from `n - 1` down to `0` — the start of the suffix being solved.
meanings.k: Inner index 0..2 choosing how many stones to take; the option value is `take - dp[i + k + 1]`, subtracting the opponent's best margin on the rest.
meanings.ans: Sign of `dp[0]`: positive → `"Alice"`, negative → `"Bob"`, zero → `"Tie"`.

title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
why: Carry the maximum value on the root-to-node path; a node is good when it reaches or exceeds that maximum.

meanings.root: root of the binary tree
meanings.node: current node visited by the DFS
meanings.count: running count of good nodes found so far
meanings.maxSoFar: largest value seen on the path from `root` down to `node`; a node is good when `node.val >= maxSoFar`

title: Course Schedule IV
why: Prerequisite reachability is transitive: reaching an intermediate course can reveal further dependent courses.

meanings.prerequisites: List of pairs `[a, b]` meaning `a` is a prerequisite of `b` (directed edge `a → b`).
meanings.queries: List of pairs `[u, v]`; each asks "is `u` a prerequisite of `v`?"
meanings.adj: Adjacency list; `adj[a]` holds every course that `a` directly unlocks.
meanings.reach: `numCourses × numCourses` boolean matrix; `reach[src][dst]` is `true` when `src` is a (direct or indirect) prerequisite of `dst`.
meanings.dfs: Depth-first search from a fixed `src`; marks `reach[src][nei]` for everything reachable.
meanings.src: The root course whose transitive descendants we are filling in.
meanings.nei: A neighbor of the current node being marked reachable from `src`.
meanings.res: Result array: `queries.map(([u, v]) => reach[u][v])`.

title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
why: Compare minimum spanning-tree cost when an edge is excluded or forced to determine its role across optimal trees.

meanings.n: Number of vertices `0 .. n-1`. A spanning tree connects all `n` of them with exactly `n - 1` edges.
meanings.edges: Input array of `[u, v, w]` weighted undirected edges. Indices into this array are what the answer reports.
meanings.indexed: `edges` rewritten as `[u, v, w, origIndex]`, then sorted ascending by weight `w`. Sorting is what makes Kruskal greedy; `origIndex` (slot 3) lets us report answers in the caller's original numbering.
meanings.dsu: A `DSU` (Disjoint Set Union / union-find) instance. `dsu.find(x)` returns x's component root (with path-halving); `dsu.union(a,b)` merges and returns `true` only if they were separate.
meanings.parent: The DSU's backing array; `parent[x]` points one step toward x's root, and a root points to itself. Snapshotted each step so Step Back is reversible.
meanings.buildMST: `(skip, force) => weight`. Runs Kruskal but (a) ignores edge `skip`, and (b) unions edge `force` first regardless of order. Returns the spanning-tree weight, or `Infinity` if the result is disconnected (`dsu.count !== 1`).
meanings.skip: Index (into `indexed`) of an edge to exclude. `buildMST(i, -1)` tests "what is the best MST without edge `i`?"
meanings.force: Index of an edge to include up front. `buildMST(-1, i)` tests "is there an MST that uses edge `i`?"
meanings.weight: Running total of accepted edge weights inside one `buildMST` run.
meanings.mstWeight: The baseline `buildMST(-1, -1)` weight — the true minimum spanning tree weight, the yardstick for every classification.
meanings.critical: Edges where `buildMST(skip=i) > mstWeight` (removing the edge raises the MST weight or disconnects the graph). Every MST must contain them.
meanings.pseudo: Edges that are not critical but where `buildMST(force=i) === mstWeight` (some MST can include them).
meanings.i: Loop index over `indexed`; identifies the edge currently being added (inside `buildMST`) or classified (in the outer loop).

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
why: Choose low-cost edges that connect previously separate parts without creating a cycle.

meanings.points: Input array of `[x, y]` coordinates; the graph is complete with edge weights = Manhattan distance `
meanings.n: Number of points (nodes). The MST has exactly `n - 1` edges and `total` is minimized.
meanings.inMST: Boolean array of length `n`; `inMST[i]` is `true` once node `i` has been pulled into the growing tree. Prim's "visited" set.
meanings.heap: A `MinHeap` of `[cost, node]` entries ordered by `cost`. Holds candidate edges crossing from the tree to outside nodes (the frontier). Stale duplicates are tolerated.
meanings.total: Running sum of the weights of edges accepted into the MST. The final answer.
meanings.count: How many nodes are in the tree so far. The loop stops once `count === n`.
meanings.cost: Weight popped off the heap for the current candidate node. Added to `total` when the node is accepted.
meanings.i: The node just popped from the heap (and being added to the tree). Its neighbors are relaxed.
meanings.j: Loop index over all nodes; for each `j` not yet `inMST`, push the distance from the new tree node `i` to `j`.
meanings.d: Manhattan distance `Math.abs(points[i][0]-points[j][0]) + Math.abs(points[i][1]-points[j][1])` — the candidate edge weight pushed as `[d, j]`.

title: Path with Minimum Effort
why: A path's effort is its largest adjacent height difference; compare routes by that maximum rather than by a sum.

meanings.heights: Input grid; `heights[r][c]` is the elevation of cell `(r, c)`.
meanings.effort: `effort[r][c]` = smallest possible "max absolute height jump" along any path from `(0,0)` to `(r, c)`; starts at `Infinity`, with `effort[0][0] = 0`.
meanings.heap: Min-heap of `[e, r, c]` ordered by effort `e` (a `class MinHeap`); pops the cell reachable with the least effort.
meanings.e: Effort popped off the heap for the current cell `(r, c)`.

title: Merge Strings Alternately
why: Alternate available characters from both strings, then append the remainder of the longer string.

meanings.i: pointer into word1
meanings.j: pointer into word2
meanings.res: array of appended characters, joined into the merged string

title: Single-Threaded CPU
why: Among arrived tasks, choose the shortest processing time and then the smallest index; jump time when none are available.

meanings.indexed: `tasks` tagged with original index `[enqueueTime, processingTime, i]`, then sorted by `enqueueTime`.
meanings.heap: Min-heap of available tasks, keyed lexicographically by `[processingTime, index]`.
meanings.time: The CPU clock; advances by a task's `processingTime`, or jumps to the next `enqueueTime` when idle.
meanings.i: Pointer into `indexed`; admits every task with `enqueueTime <= time` into the heap.
meanings.res: Output order: indices of tasks in the sequence the CPU runs them.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
why: For each ordered query, retain covering intervals and select the shortest one that has not expired.

meanings.intervals: Array of `[left, right]` intervals, sorted ascending by start.
meanings.queries: The query points, answered in their original order in the output.
meanings.sortedQueries: `[q, idx]` pairs sorted by `q`; lets us sweep queries left to right (offline).
meanings.res: Answer array, filled with `-1`; `res[idx]` gets the smallest covering size per original index.
meanings.heap: Min-heap of `[size, end]` for intervals whose start `<= q`; ordered by interval size.
meanings.i: Pointer into `intervals`; only moves forward as queries increase.

title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
why: Each include/exclude path determines one subset's XOR; add its completed XOR to the total.

meanings.nums: input array of numbers
meanings.ans: running sum of every subset's XOR total (the answer)
meanings.i: index of the element this dfs frame decides (take or skip)
meanings.xorSoFar: XOR of all elements taken on the path to the current node

title: Jump Game VII
why: Only reachable zero positions within the allowed jump-distance window can make the current position reachable.

meanings.s: Binary string of `'0'`/`'1'`; you may only stand on `'0'` cells and start at index 0.
meanings.minJump: Minimum jump length; from index `i` you may reach indices `i + minJump .. i + maxJump`.
meanings.n: `s.length`.
meanings.dp: Boolean array; `dp[i]` is `true` iff index `i` is reachable from the start.
meanings.windowCount: Number of reachable cells (`dp = true`) currently inside the sliding window `[i - maxJump, i - minJump]`.
meanings.i: Loop pointer scanning indices `1 .. n - 1`.
meanings.ans: Final boolean `dp[n - 1]`: whether the last index is reachable.

title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
why: Discard triplets that exceed any target coordinate; the remaining triplets must collectively supply every target coordinate.

meanings.triplets: List of `[x, y, z]` triplet rows we may merge with max()
meanings.target: The triplet `[t0, t1, t2]` we are trying to build
meanings.a: Flag: some usable triplet has its first component equal to target[0]
meanings.b: Flag: some usable triplet has its second component equal to target[1]
meanings.c: Flag: some usable triplet has its third component equal to target[2]
meanings.x, y, z: The three components of the current triplet being examined
meanings.ans: Final result: `a && b && c`

title: Concatenation of Array
why: Each input value is copied to its original index and to that index plus the input length.

meanings.nums: input array
meanings.res: concatenated output
meanings.i: loop index
meanings.n: length of nums

title: Detect Squares
why: A diagonal partner fixes the other two square corners; multiply occurrence counts to include duplicate points.

meanings.counts: `Map` from `"x,y"` key to multiplicity (how many times that point was added).
meanings.point: The `[x, y]` argument passed to `add()` or `count()`.
meanings.key: String form `point[0] + "," + point[1]` used as the Map key.
meanings.res: Running total of squares: `res += c1 * c2 * c3` over every valid diagonal.

title: Build a Matrix With Conditions
why: Independent topological orders determine row and column positions; either dependency cycle prevents a solution.

meanings.k: The matrix is `k × k` and must contain each value `1..k` exactly once, with the remaining cells set to 0.
meanings.rowConditions: Pairs `[a, b]` meaning value `a` must appear in an **earlier row** than value `b`. Fed into the first topological sort.
meanings.colConditions: Pairs `[a, b]` meaning value `a` must appear in an **earlier column** than value `b`. Fed into the second, independent topological sort.
meanings.adj: Adjacency list built inside `topo(conditions)`: `adj[a]` lists every value that must come after `a` along the current axis.
meanings.indeg: Indegree array for the current axis. A value with indegree 0 has no predecessor left and can be placed next; Kahn's algorithm decrements indegrees as nodes are removed.
meanings.order: The topological order produced for one axis. Its index is the position: `order[i] = v` means value `v` takes slot `i` on that axis. If `order.length !== k`, that axis has a cycle and `topo` returns `null`.
meanings.rowPos: `Map<value, rowIndex>` derived from `rowOrder` — the row each value occupies.
meanings.colPos: `Map<value, colIndex>` derived from `colOrder` — the column each value occupies.
meanings.matrix: The `k × k` result, initialized to all zeros. Each value `v` is written at `matrix[rowPos[v]][colPos[v]]`. Returned as `[]` if either axis was impossible.
meanings.v: The value `1..k` currently being placed into the matrix at its `(rowPos[v], colPos[v])` cell.

title: Meeting Rooms III
why: Use an available room when possible; otherwise delay the meeting until the earliest room release while preserving duration.

meanings.n: Number of meeting rooms, indexed `0 .. n-1`.
meanings.meetings: Array of `[start, end]` meetings, sorted ascending by start time.
meanings.count: `count[r]` = how many meetings room `r` has hosted (the booking counter).
meanings.available: Sorted list of free room indices; lowest index is taken first.
meanings.busy: List of `[endTime, room]` for rooms in use, kept sorted by end time (ties by room).
meanings.room: The room chosen for the current meeting (freed, assigned, or waited for).
meanings.freeTime: When the earliest-freeing busy room becomes available (used when all rooms are busy).
meanings.best: Index of the busiest room so far; the final answer (lowest index wins ties).
meanings.r: Loop index over rooms (initial fill and final scan for the busiest room).

title: Extra Characters in a String
why: At each string position, compare skipping an extra character with consuming a matching dictionary word.

meanings.s: The input string we are trying to break into dictionary words.
meanings.dictionary: The list of valid words; any substring of `s` matching one is "covered".
meanings.root: Root `TrieNode` of the trie built from every word in `dictionary`.
meanings.node: The current `TrieNode` while inserting a word or while walking `s[i..j]`.
meanings.ch: The current character: `s[j]` during the DP scan (or a letter of a word during insert).
meanings.dp: Suffix DP array of length `n + 1`; `dp[i]` = minimum extra chars for the suffix `s[i..]`. `dp[n] = 0`.
meanings.i: Outer DP index, iterating right → left. `dp[i] = dp[i+1] + 1` is the "skip `s[i]`" default.
meanings.j: Inner index walking forward from `i`; `s[i..j]` is the substring matched against the trie.
meanings.ans: The final answer, `dp[0]` — the minimum number of leftover (extra) characters.

title: Greatest Common Divisor Traversal
why: A shared prime factor connects values; transitive factor connections determine whether every value is reachable.

meanings.nums: Input array. Two indices may be traversed between when `gcd(nums[i], nums[j]) > 1`, i.e. they share a prime factor.
meanings.n: Length of `nums`; also the number of nodes in the union-find.
meanings.dsu: `class DSU` disjoint-set. Each index starts in its own component; `union` merges components that share a prime. `dsu.count` tracks how many components remain.
meanings.parent: The `dsu.parent` array. `parent[x]` is `x`'s parent; following it to a fixed point gives the component root. Path compression flattens it during `find`.
meanings.primeToIndex: `Map` from a prime `p` to the **first** node index that contained `p`. The second node to see `p` unions itself with that owner.
meanings.i: Index of the node currently being factored.
meanings.x: Working copy of `nums[i]` that is divided down as prime factors are extracted; any leftover `> 1` is itself a prime.
meanings.p: Trial-division candidate. The loop runs while `p * p <= x`.

title: Insert Greatest Common Divisors in Linked List
why: Insert the greatest common divisor between each original adjacent pair without skipping the next original pair.

meanings.head: Head node of the input linked list (also returned at the end).
meanings.gcd: Recursive Euclid helper: `gcd(a, b) = b === 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b)`.
meanings.curr: Walking pointer; sits on the left node of the current consecutive pair.
meanings.node: The freshly created `ListNode` holding `gcd(curr.val, curr.next.val)`.
meanings.ListNode: ES6 class node: `constructor(val, next = null)` with `this.val` and `this.next`.

title: Minimum Array End
why: Preserve x's set bits and place the bits of n−1 into its zero positions to obtain the smallest possible final value.

meanings.n: Number of array elements. The last (largest) element is the `(n - 1)`-th value above `x`.
meanings.x: Required AND-mask. Every element must contain all of `x`'s set bits, so the answer starts from `x`.
meanings.result: The minimum last element, built as a `BigInt`. Starts at `x`; free (zero) bit slots get filled from `remaining`. Returned as a `Number`.
meanings.remaining: `BigInt(n - 1)`. Its bits are distributed, lowest-first, into the zero-bit positions of `result`.
meanings.bit: One-hot `BigInt` cursor (`1n`, then `<< 1n` each step) marking the bit position currently under inspection.

title: Path Sum III
why: A matching downward path is the difference between two prefixes on one ancestor branch. Count every matching prefix, then remove the current occurrence before returning so siblings cannot share it.

meanings.root: original root of the input tree
meanings.targetSum: required sum of a nonempty downward path
meanings.node: node in the current recursive call, or null for an absent child
meanings.sum: prefix sum in this call, passed by value to its children
meanings.matches: number of earlier matching prefixes read before insertion
meanings.freq: Map from ancestor prefix sums to their occurrence counts
meanings.count: total matching paths counted across the tree

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
why: An edge must join opposite groups. Assign a vertex before enqueueing it, inspect every component, and stop at the first edge whose endpoints have the same label.

meanings.graph: original zero-based undirected adjacency list; each row keeps its node identity
meanings.n: number of vertices, including isolated vertices
meanings.color: 0 means unassigned; +1 and -1 name the two groups
meanings.start: next vertex checked by the outer component scan
meanings.queue: vertices discovered in this component, retained in insertion order
meanings.head: index of the next queue entry to read; earlier entries are already dequeued
meanings.node: vertex currently being expanded
meanings.i: index of the next neighbor in graph[node]
meanings.neighbor: neighbor read for this one edge check
